kind_of_thing.quote: Momordica charantia (commonly called bitter melon, gouya,  cerassee, goya, bitter apple, bitter gourd, bitter squash, balsam-pear, karela, karavila and many more names listed below) is a tropical and subtropical vine of the family Cucurbitaceae, widely grown in Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean for its edible fruit.

extinct.why: The sources describe it as a widely grown, currently used food plant, so it is still living.

kind_of_plant.why: It is a vine grown for its edible fruit, which is widely used as a vegetable in cooking.
